name: Text as a whole
title: REPORT on the amended proposal for a Decision of the European Parliament and of the Council amending Council Decision 2008/971/EC as regards the forest reproductive material of the ‘tested’ category, its labelling and the names of the authorities responsible for the approval and control of the production
part_text:
The European Union lets in tree seeds and young trees from seven countries outside it — Canada, Norway, Serbia, Switzerland, Türkiye, the United Kingdom and the United States — if they meet EU rules. This report adds a fourth quality class, called "tested", to the classes already accepted. It also updates the list of foreign authorities that certify the material and requires labels to say whether genetic modification was used. The aim is to keep imports flowing after the current temporary arrangement ends on 31 December 2024.

- The "tested" class of tree seeds and young trees from those seven countries is now accepted as equivalent to EU material.
- It affects nurseries, foresters and traders importing forest reproductive material, plus the foreign authorities that certify it.
- The new rules apply from 1 January 2025, once the decision is formally adopted and published.
